fullPassage: In a classic study from 1975, Ellen Langer and Jane Roth trained 90 Stanford undergraduate students to play a coin-flip game. Students who guessed correctly early were much more likely to decide that they were correctly predicting the outcomes than students who guessed incorrectly early. That is, a sequence of wins followed by losses led the students to imagine they understood the task and needed to try to figure out what was going wrong, while a series of losses intermixed with wins led the students to think it was random. A sequence of four correct early guesses was enough to lead people to believe they could correctly guess the sequence "even for sophisticated subjects." This is how the casinos hook people — a quick series of wins leads you to think that you can beat the game, even though WWWWWLLLLL (where W means win and L means lose) is just as random as WLWLLLWWLW.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: understand → understood: 과거 시제 불규칙 변화
det.analysis: understand(현재) → understood(과거). 주절 동사 led, needed가 과거 시제이므로 종속절도 과거 시제로 일치시켜야 함. 학생들이 과제를 '이해했다'고 상상한 것이므로 과거형 understood
det.tip: understand-understood-understood (불규칙). 시제 일치로 과거형

questions.passage: In a classic study from 1975, Ellen Langer and Jane Roth trained 90 Stanford undergraduate students to play a __________. Students who guessed correctly early were much more likely to decide that they were correctly predicting the outcomes than students who guessed incorrectly early. That is, a sequence of wins followed by losses led the students to imagine they understood the task and needed to try to figure out what was going wrong, while a series of losses intermixed with wins led the students to think it was random. A sequence of four correct early guesses was enough to lead people to believe they could correctly guess the sequence "even for sophisticated subjects." This is how the casinos hook people — a quick series of wins leads you to think that you can beat the game, even though WWWWWLLLLL (where W means win and L means lose) is just as random as WLWLLLWWLW.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① board puzzle(보드 퍼즐): 승패·확률 문맥과 거리가 멂
❌ ② card trick(카드 마술): 예측·무작위성 문맥과 다름
❌ ③ math quiz(수학 퀴즈): 운·무작위성과 무관
✅ ④ coin-flip game(동전 던지기 게임): 승패와 무작위성을 다루는 게임 ← 정답
det.tip: coin-flip game=동전 던지기 게임. 승/패(W/L)와 무작위성의 소재

det.korean: 연속된 승리는 당신이 ______ 수 있다고 생각하게 만든다
det.analysis:
✅ ① beat the game(게임을 이기다): 승리의 연속이 이길 수 있다는 착각을 줌 ← 정답
❌ ② count the cards(카드를 세다): 동전 게임과 무관
❌ ③ read the dealer(딜러를 읽다): 본문에 근거 없음
❌ ④ leave the table(테이블을 떠나다): 끌어들이는 심리와 반대
det.tip: beat the game=게임을 이기다. 통제의 착각(illusion of control)의 핵심 표현
